title: Runtime Cost Estimation and Model Introspection API Standards
author: Marco Nguyen
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a cross-cutting API standard for lightweight model introspection and runtime cost estimation endpoints. The goal is to provide a predictable, machine-readable contract that clients (SDKs, Console, autoscalers, and billing pipeline) can rely on to estimate token-level cost, latency, and capability signals before issuing full inference requests.

Why this exists
----------------
- Reduce end-to-end uncertainty in per-request cost estimation (important for routing and preflight charging).
- Allow clients to select model variants (quantized vs full-precision) and routing lanes based on a standard cost/latency signal.
- Provide identical, discoverable metadata across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Support safe, backward-compatible evolution of runtime cost heuristics.

Design Goals
------------
1. Minimal performance impact on runtime: introspection endpoints should be cheap and cacheable.
2. Deterministic semantics: fields have explicit units and confidence levels.
3. Versioned responses with feature flags for rollout.
4. Authentication, rate limits, and SLOs aligned with other control-plane APIs.
5. Clear deprecation and compatibility policy.

API Contract (stable v1)
------------------------
Base path (example): GET /v1/models/{model_id}/introspect
               POST /v1/models/{model_id}/estimate-cost

Authentication & Authorization
- Use the same bearer token scheme as /v1/requests. Tokens must carry scope: models:introspect for read access.
- Rate limits and quota: default 60 req/min per API key for introspect endpoints (can be tuned per-tier).

Introspect (GET) - purpose: capability discovery and static metadata
Request: GET /v1/models/gpt-xxl/introspect?region=us-west-2&variant=auto
Successful response (application/json) - 200 OK
{
  "model_id": "gpt-xxl",
  "variant": "q4_k_mixed",                    // string - variant identifier
  "artifact_version": "2026-02-18-rc3",       // string - build tag
  "max_context_tokens": 131072,                 // integer
  "supports_streaming": true,                   // boolean
  "supports_function_calling": false,           // boolean
  "native_quantization_profiles": ["q4_k_mixed", "q8_0"], // list<string>
  "annotation": "inference:float32_main_gpu | optimizer:v2" // freeform short note
}
Notes:
- All timestamps in annotations should be ISO-8601 when present.
- Response should be cacheable for up to 24 hours unless artifact_version changes.

Estimate-Cost (POST) - purpose: workload-specific estimated cost/latency
Request: POST /v1/models/gpt-xxl/estimate-cost
Content-Type: application/json
Body (example):
{
  "prompt_tokens": 256,
  "expected_generate_tokens": 512,
  "topology_hints": {"gpu":"a100-80g","region":"us-west-2"},
  "features": ["streaming"],
  "preferred_variant": "q4_k_mixed",
  "trace_id": "client-7890-req-1"
}
Response (application/json) - 200 OK
{
  "model_id": "gpt-xxl",
  "variant": "q4_k_mixed",
  "estimator_version": "cost-v1.2",
  "estimated_cost_usd": 0.00234,          // float - USD for the entire request
  "cost_per_token_usd": 0.00000246,        // float - USD per generated token
  "estimated_latency_ms": 289.1,          // float - median latency in ms for full generation
  "latency_distribution_ms": {"p50": 240.0, "p90": 400.0, "p99": 900.0}, // map (see notes)
  "confidence": 0.86,                      // float 0..1
  "assumptions": ["no-kv-cache","seq_len=1024"],
  "advice": "switch-to-q8_0 for lower latency at similar cost" // human-readable hint
}
Notes on fields:
- All currency values are USD and must be returned as numbers with at most 8 decimal places. Billing pipelines may reformat.
- estimated_latency_ms is the expected wall-clock time for the full request given the provided hints.
- latency_distribution_ms is intended to be small JSON object with keys 'p50','p90','p99' numeric ms. If not available, omit the field.
- confidence is a unitless heuristic (0..1) representing estimator certainty; owners should provide guidance for thresholds used in automated routing.

Error model
-----------
- 4xx responses follow the canonical error shape used in other API standards: {"code":"BadRequest","message":"...","details":[]}
- 429 for rate-limit, 403 for insufficient scope, 502/503 for runtime unavailability.

Cache and freshness semantics
---------------------------
- Introspect responses: Cache-Control: max-age=86400 unless artifact_version absent. Presence of artifact_version implies immutable content.
- Estimate-Cost responses: Cache only when estimator_version is stable and the request repeatability is high. Suggested default: 30s TTL for identical requests.

SLOs and operational requirements
--------------------------------
- Introspect endpoints: P95 latency <= 50ms; availability >= 99.95% (regional).
- Estimate-Cost endpoints: P95 latency <= 150ms for simple estimates (no kernel probing); availability >= 99.9%.
- Monitoring: metric names must follow the conventions in observability standards: api.introspect.latency_ms, api.estimate_cost.latency_ms, api.introspect.errors, api.estimate_cost.confidence_distribution.
- Alerting: fire when error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m or P95 latency breaches SLO for 15m.

Versioning and evolution policy
------------------------------
1. Use a semantic estimator_version field in responses. Client behavior should prefer the version indicated.
2. Non-breaking additions (new optional fields) are allowed within the same major contract.
3. Breaking changes require publication of new major path (e.g., /v2/models/...) and an ADR with migration plan and at least 30 days of dual support.
4. Deprecation lifecycle: announce (30d) -> soft-deprecate (read-only warnings, 60d) -> removal (after 90d unless approved longer by product security).

Compatibility rules for private deployments
-----------------------------------------
- Private (VPC/on-prem) control planes may return a specialized estimator_version; the same contract must be honored. If local estimators are not present, the runtime must return a 503 with a standard hint header X-Estimator-Fallback: none.

Security and privacy
--------------------
- Request bodies should not contain PII. If policy-determined features require telemetry, the introspect endpoints must honor the customer's data-residency and redaction policies.
- Introspect responses may be logged but must be filtered for tenant identifiers when forwarded to shared telemetry.

Operational runbook (quick)
--------------------------
1. Symptom: estimate-cost latency spikes.
   - Check api.estimate_cost.latency_ms dashboards by region and estimator_version.
   - Verify estimator service pod health and recent deployments.
   - If estimator_version recently changed, roll back using the artifact tag in deployment pipeline.
2. Symptom: confidence<0.3 for many requests.
   - Check training/telemetry coverage for the estimator version.
   - If underprovisioned, route estimations to a stronger estimator (see routing policy below).

Routing guidance and automated fallback
-------------------------------------
- Primary decision factors for routing: (cost_priority, latency_budget_ms, availability).
- If confidence < 0.5 and estimated_latency_ms > latency_budget_ms -> route to alternate variant with lower estimated_latency_ms.
- If estimator responds 503 or fails, default to conservative static cost table (maintained in config repo) and tag telemetry with estimator:fallback.

Owner and SLAs
--------------
- Ownership: Runtime Cost & Discovery subteam (primary), Runtime Platform (secondary).
- Contact alias: runtime-cost@redwood.ai
- SLA: the estimator endpoints are tracked under service id runtime-estimator; see SLO dashboard runtime-estimator/slo-2026.

Testing and conformance
-----------------------
- Unit tests for estimators must include deterministic fixtures and seed-based RNGs.
- Integration tests: a conformance test harness will POST 100 representative payloads and validate field types, units, and response time budget.
- Gate: All major changes require an entry in the performance regression suite with 95% coverage for latency buckets.

Appendix: example curl and SDK snippets
---------------------------------------
curl example:
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/gpt-xxl/estimate-cost\" \
  -d '{"prompt_tokens":128, "expected_generate_tokens":256}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
SDK (python pseudo):
```
est = client.models.estimate_cost('gpt-xxl', prompt_tokens=128, expected_generate_tokens=256)
print(est.estimated_cost_usd, est.confidence)
```

References and related standards
--------------------------------
- See observability SLI naming and ingestion rules: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/granular-metrics-taxonomy-and-dimension-catalog-2026.json
- See model capability manifest standard for additional discovery fields: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/model-capability-manifest-runtime-discovery-2026.json
